pr.title: Post the `projector/review` status on the version-only release commit
pr.head: 39fceb4fc4057848097827c9811078ac336b17d3

summary: A trip release is a pull request that the Release workflow opens for you. It raises the version in Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock and changes nothing else. When you merge it, the workflow tags and publishes the release.

main now has a ruleset that requires a commit status named projector/review before a pull request can merge. A Projector review normally posts that status after it reads the head. No review session picks up a pull request that the workflow's own token opened, so release 0.2.2 sat waiting for a status that nothing would post.

This pull request makes the workflow's propose job post projector/review as success itself. It posts the status only on the commit that check-commit has just proved changes nothing but the version. The status belongs to that one commit, so if anyone pushes to the release branch, the new head has no status and needs a real review before it can merge.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Commit status: a state (success, failure, pending) that GitHub attaches to one commit SHA under a name called its context.
  • projector/review: the context the "Projector review" ruleset requires on main.
  • Propose job: the Release workflow job you start by hand. It bumps the version, pushes release/vX.Y.Z, and opens the pull request.
  • check-commit: the release.py command that refuses a commit unless it raises the version and changes nothing else.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One Projector review, of 39fceb4: clean, with no findings and no suggestions.
  • python3 tests/release_test.py ran 30 tests, all passing, on this head.

groups.title: The propose job signs off its own commit
groups.kicker: One new API call in the Release workflow, and the permission it needs
intro: After the propose job commits the version bump, it runs check-commit HEAD and force-pushes the release branch. Next, it now calls the commit statuses API on $(git rev-parse HEAD), posting projector/review as success with a link to the run. Only then does it open the pull request. The job gains statuses: write so that its GITHUB_TOKEN can make the call.

The sign-off is safe only because of what check-commit compares. It diffs the release commit against its parent alone, and the job refuses to run from any ref but main. So the parent is main's reviewed head, and the one new commit can hold only the version change.

checks.text: The live "Projector review" ruleset, read with gh api repos/ninjudd/trip/rulesets, requires the projector/review context with no integration_id. So a status that GITHUB_TOKEN posts satisfies it, as the pull request body says.
The change grants nobody a new power. Anyone who can dispatch this workflow already has write access to the repository, and with it the power to post commit statuses.

files.note: Adds statuses: write and the status call between git push and gh pr create, and updates the pull request body template.

checks.text: The main-only guard now protects the sign-off too. A run from another ref would carry that ref's unreviewed commits onto the release branch, and this step would mark them reviewed.
The status targets a fixed SHA, not the branch, so a commit someone pushes after the force-push gets no success. Under set -euo pipefail, a failed call stops the step before the pull request opens.

files.note: The module docstring now lists the status step in the workflow's sequence.

groups.title: Test and documentation
groups.kicker: A test of the step's order, and the README's release section
intro: The new test reads the propose job's text out of release.yml and checks the order of its steps, as the test above it already does for the version check. The README's release section now explains why the workflow posts the status and what a later push to the release branch needs.

files.note: The test fails if the status call moves before check-commit or git push, appears twice, targets anything but HEAD, or loses its permission.

checks.text: The author confirmed that it fails when the status step moves above check-commit and when the permission is removed. The suite passes on this head.

files.note: The release section says that the workflow signs off the version-only commit, and that a push to the release branch needs a Projector review.

checks.text: docs/projects/releases/readme.md still says that the propose job posts no status. That plan is completed and stands as a record, so the README is the living document that this change updates.
